entries.title: Sources has a new Investigate view
entries.body: For articles you own, Sources has a new view, Investigate: ask your own question, or a suggested one, about what others say of the piece, whether its claims hold up, or the works it cites, and Chat opens to search the web for an answer. The question box that sat in Reception has moved here, beside a list of your earlier questions. Reception is easier to scan: the AI's groupings start folded above a list of every page found, and each source is one short row until you open it.

entries.title: Export everything you wrote about an article
entries.body: An article's details page has a new download, also added to the article's export: one readable file of your own words, with your title, purpose and tags, your comments in article order, your quiz answers and nearly all your conversations, the AI's replies labelled. Each conversation also has a button to copy it as Markdown, plain text that pastes cleanly into a document or another AI. The details page also says plainly whether the article is yours.

entries.title: Learn's Tutorial is now part of Recall
entries.body: Learn now has Recall, Explore and Quiz. Tutorial has been folded into Recall, which takes you through a piece you have not read yet a small part at a time, pointing to the passages as it goes. Your Tutorial conversations now sit under Recall with nothing you wrote deleted, and old Tutorial links open Recall.

entries.title: Chat offers to remember lasting preferences
entries.body: When you tell Chat or Learn's Explore something lasting, such as to keep answers brief, a card beneath the answer offers to add it to About you; nothing is saved until you press it, and your latest request still outranks a saved preference. Chat, Recall and Explore also always use the more capable AI, whatever the High-powered AI setting.

entries.title: Help has one box to search and ask
entries.body: Help's separate search and question boxes are now one, and matching pages are listed as you type. Signed in, press Ask or Enter and the AI answers above the matches; signed out, Enter opens the best match.

entries.title: Dictate into the boxes when adding an article
entries.body: Both boxes on the page for adding an article, Why are you reading this? and About you, have a microphone, so you can say your answer instead of typing it. While you are dictating, the page waits for you rather than moving on to the article.

entries.title: Structure draws a ribbon between its columns
entries.body: When Structure shows two columns, a curved grey band joins the current part to its sections in the second column, and the part is shaded to match. It makes plain which sections belong to which part, and it redraws as the window or text size changes.

entries.title: Chat handles mid-answer rewrites and long conversations
entries.body: A question rewritten while its answer was still arriving was refused until you stopped the answer; pressing Ask again now stops it and asks the new question. Asked to read another of your conversations, Chat and Explore saw only its latest ten exchanges, each cut short; they can now page back to the start, or say they did not.
